title: The k-th Lexicographical String of All Happy Strings of Length n
summary: A happy string is formed by letters 'a', 'b', and 'c' with no consecutive identical characters.
statement: A happy string is formed by letters 'a', 'b', and 'c' with no consecutive identical characters. Given integers n and k, find the k-th lexicographically ordered happy string of length n, or return an empty string if fewer than k such strings exist.
constraints: A happy string uses only a, b, c and has no equal adjacent characters.
Return the one-based kth string in lexicographic order, or empty when k is too large.
hints: Build candidates left-to-right in a, b, c order.
Skip a character equal to the current last character.
Each completed length-n path arrives in lexicographic order.
Select index k-1 when present; otherwise the requested rank does not exist.
editorial: Select index k-1 when present; otherwise the requested rank does not exist.

tests.explanation: The length-one order is a, b, c, so the third is c.
There are twelve length-three happy strings; the ninth is cab.
